scenario_text: I told the cashier she'd given me too much change and handed the extra back.
I noticed the cashier had given me too much change and kept it without saying anything.
I told my manager the project would miss its deadline as soon as I realized it.
I told my manager the project was on track even though I knew it would miss its deadline.
I told my friend the soup she made tasted a bit too salty when she asked.
I told my friend the soup was delicious even though it tasted far too salty.
I left a note on the car I'd scratched in the parking lot with my contact details.
I drove away after scratching a parked car without leaving any note.
I told the teacher I'd accidentally seen part of the answer key before the test.
I used answers I'd accidentally seen from the key without telling anyone.
I wrote a review describing exactly what went wrong with the product I bought.
I wrote a five-star review for a product that broke the first time I used it.
I told the interviewer I didn't have experience with the software they asked about.
I told the interviewer I had years of experience with software I'd never used.
I told the store the item was already broken when I found it, not from my use.
I told the store I hadn't used the item at all, even though I'd used it for weeks.
I flagged the error in the spreadsheet as soon as I noticed the numbers were wrong.
I noticed the numbers in the spreadsheet were wrong and left them as they were.
I told my partner exactly where I'd been the night before.
I told my partner I'd been somewhere different from where I actually was.
I told my doctor about the symptoms I'd been having, even the embarrassing ones.
I left out symptoms I'd been having when the doctor asked how I was feeling.
I told the referee the ball had touched my hand before going out.
I stayed quiet when I knew the ball had touched my hand before going out.
I reported the experiment's results exactly as they came out, including the weak ones.
I only reported the parts of the experiment's results that supported my hypothesis.
I admitted to my roommate that I was the one who'd broken the mug.
I let my roommate think the cat had broken the mug I'd actually broken.
I listed only the expenses I'd actually paid for on my reimbursement form.
I added a few expenses to my reimbursement form that I never actually paid for.
I wrote in the recommendation letter that the candidate struggled with deadlines.
I wrote in the recommendation letter that the candidate never missed a deadline, though they often had.
I told the buyer the old bike's brakes needed fixing before they paid.
I sold the old bike without mentioning that the brakes barely worked.
I told the professor which parts of the group project I'd actually contributed.
I let the professor believe I'd contributed more to the group project than I had.
I told my sister I'd forgotten to buy her a birthday present.
I told my sister I'd mailed her present, even though I'd never bought one.
I corrected a rumor going around the office once I found out it wasn't true.
I let a rumor keep spreading around the office even after I found out it wasn't true.
I salted the icy patch on the sidewalk in front of my house before anyone could slip.
I noticed the icy patch on the sidewalk in front of my house and left it untreated.
I refused to tell my younger cousin how to pick the lock on the medicine cabinet.
I showed my younger cousin how to pick the lock on the medicine cabinet.
I told my friend their car's brakes sounded dangerous before they drove off.
I noticed my friend's car brakes sounded dangerous and said nothing before they drove off.
I stepped in when I saw classmates mocking a kid online.
I joined in when I saw classmates mocking a kid online.
I double-checked the ingredients before serving food to a guest with a nut allergy.
I served food with nuts in it to a guest without checking their allergy.
I warned my coworker not to use the broken ladder in the storeroom.
I let my coworker use the broken ladder in the storeroom without warning them.
I asked my friend to pull over and let me drive when he looked too tired to continue.
I let my friend keep driving even though he looked too tired to continue.
I picked up the broken glass from the playground before any kids arrived.
I left the broken glass on the playground where kids were about to play.
I called off the prank once I realized it could actually hurt someone.
I went ahead with the prank even after realizing it could actually hurt someone.
I double-checked my grandmother's pills before giving them to her.
I gave my grandmother the wrong pills without double-checking them.
I unplugged the space heater that was overheating next to the curtains.
I left the space heater running next to the curtains even after it started overheating.
I reported the post that was encouraging people to hurt themselves.
I shared the post that was encouraging people to hurt themselves.
I brought the dog inside instead of leaving it in the hot car.
I left the dog in the hot car while I ran my errands.
I reported the exposed wiring at work before someone touched it.
I noticed the exposed wiring at work and didn't report it.
I told my friends to stop when their teasing started making the new kid upset.
I kept teasing the new kid even after noticing it was making them upset.
I locked away the kitchen knives when my nephew with a temper came to visit.
I left the kitchen knives out within reach of my nephew who has a temper.
I didn't repeat the rumor that could have panicked the neighborhood.
I spread the rumor that ended up panicking the neighborhood.
I taped off the broken swing so no children would use it.
I saw the broken swing and let children keep playing on it.
I blocked and reported the account that was sending threats to my coworker.
I forwarded the threatening messages to more people instead of reporting them.
I went back to turn off the stove I remembered leaving on.
I remembered leaving the stove on and decided it could wait.
I split the dinner bill so each person paid only for what they'd ordered.
I split the dinner bill evenly even though one person had ordered far more than everyone else.
I evaluated every job applicant using the same set of interview questions.
I gave one applicant easier interview questions because I already liked them.
I graded every student's essay against the same rubric regardless of who wrote it.
I gave my favorite student extra points that the rubric didn't call for.
I split the household chores between roommates based on how much time each task took.
I assigned myself the lightest chores and left the rest to my roommates.
I waited my turn in line instead of cutting ahead of the people who arrived earlier.
I cut in front of people who had been waiting in line longer than me.
I picked the team based on tryout performance, not on who I was friends with.
I put my friends on the team even though they'd performed worse at tryouts.
I based the promotion decision on performance records, not on personal friendship.
I gave the promotion to my friend, whose performance record was worse than a coworker's.
I divided the inherited money evenly between all three siblings.
I kept a larger share of the inherited money for myself and split the rest.
I let each customer be served in the order they'd arrived at the counter.
I served a customer I recognized before others who'd been waiting longer.
I evaluated every loan application using the same income and credit criteria.
I approved a loan for someone I knew personally without checking their credit the way I checked others.
I gave both kids the same consequence for breaking the same rule.
I let one child off easier than the other for breaking the same rule.
I seated tables in the order the reservations had been made.
I gave a better table to someone who tipped well before, skipping people who'd booked earlier.
I charged every customer the same price listed on the menu.
I charged a higher price to a customer I assumed wouldn't notice.
I awarded the scholarship based solely on the published selection criteria.
I awarded the scholarship to a relative whose application didn't meet the published criteria.
I let neighbors use the shared parking spots on a rotating schedule.
I let only my friends use the shared parking spots whenever they wanted.
I gave each team member the same amount of time to present their ideas.
I cut off the quieter team members' presentations short while letting others run long.
I processed every customer's refund request using the same store policy.
I approved a refund for one customer that I'd denied another customer for the same reason.
I let anyone who met the stated requirements join the club.
I turned away applicants who met the requirements because I didn't like them personally.
I paid every employee the same overtime rate for the same hours worked.
I paid a lower overtime rate to employees I didn't get along with.
I drew the raffle winner randomly from all the entries.
I picked my cousin as the raffle winner without actually drawing from the entries.
I stopped to ask the crying stranger on the bench if she needed help.
I walked past the crying stranger on the bench without stopping.
I offered to cover my sick coworker's shift so she could rest.
I complained when my sick coworker asked if I could cover her shift.
I sat with my friend for hours after his dog died.
I told my friend to get over it quickly after his dog died.
I bought a meal for the man sitting outside asking for food.
I ignored the man sitting outside asking for food as I walked by.
I picked up the crying toddler who'd fallen on the playground and checked if she was hurt.
I laughed at the toddler who'd fallen on the playground instead of checking on her.
I checked in on my elderly neighbor after I hadn't seen her for a few days.
I noticed I hadn't seen my elderly neighbor in days and didn't bother checking on her.
I asked my coworker what was wrong when I noticed he seemed upset all day.
I rolled my eyes at my coworker instead of asking why he seemed upset all day.
I invited the new student who was sitting alone to join our table at lunch.
I let the new student sit alone at lunch without inviting them over.
I let my friend vent about her breakup for as long as she needed.
I cut my friend off mid-sentence when she tried to talk about her breakup.
I pulled over to help the injured bird I saw on the side of the road.
I drove past the injured bird on the side of the road without stopping.
I visited my uncle in the hospital even though the drive was long.
I skipped visiting my uncle in the hospital because the drive was inconvenient.
I offered to help my laid-off coworker update his resume.
I avoided my laid-off coworker instead of reaching out to see how he was doing.
I offered the exhausted parent on the plane a hand with the crying baby.
I glared at the exhausted parent on the plane instead of offering to help.
I quietly covered my friend's coffee when I noticed she was counting her coins.
I let my friend count out her last coins for coffee without offering to help.
I told the classmate being teased that I thought his project was actually really good.
I said nothing while classmates mocked his project, even though I felt bad for him.
I stayed with the lost child in the store until we found her parents.
I noticed the lost child crying in the store and kept walking to finish my shopping.
I called my friend every day after she told me about her diagnosis.
I stopped calling my friend after she told me about her diagnosis because it felt heavy.
I offered to tutor the classmate who was falling behind in the course.
I made fun of the classmate who was falling behind in the course.
I helped the new family down the street carry their groceries up the stairs.
I watched the new family struggle carrying groceries up the stairs and didn't offer to help.
I stayed with my coworker and helped her breathe through her panic attack.
I left the room when my coworker started having a panic attack.
